title: kbmon's sessions panel probes a dispatch worker's pid with os.kill(pid, 0) on Windows, which ends the process
goal: on Windows the sessions panel never calls os.kill on any pid: the live-workers test of session_rows takes the same os.name guard as dispatch_runs and the synthetic-worker branch, so a sprint runner's step reads without probing its workers there
notes: SP-razcgjsb review 2026-10-20: _tools/mon_sessions.py session_rows computes live_workers = any(bl_procs.running(w) ...) with no os.name != 'nt' guard, while dispatch_runs and the synthetic-worker branch have one; bl_procs.running is os.kill(pid, 0), which on Windows ends the process (dispatch_runs' own docstring). Introduced by ST-wubbd6ws. Repro: os.name patched to nt for bl_procs and mon_sessions, os.kill spied, one claude process and one ledger record with a worker_pid: one os.kill call recorded.
